blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

# ── Target resolution ───────────────────────────────…

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Install the Dart SDK — cached, channel-aware provisioner for machine-factory
# leg sessions (gh-918).
#
# WHY: factory legs (dev/review/rework) on Dart repos had NO dart SDK on PATH —
# they could not run `dart analyze/test/format` or `crap4dart check`, so they
# could neither see nor verify quality-gate violations (CRAP / method_size /
# format) and claimed success while violations stayed in place. Same pattern
# as the golden-test Flutter toolchain for fa legs: the SDK is cached per
# resolved version and exposed on PATH for the leg session, resolving the SAME
# channel (and pinned version, when CI pins one) the checked-out repo's
# quality workflow uses — the `dart-lang/setup-dart` step's `channel:`/`sdk:`
# inputs in `.github/workflows/*.yml`. The SDK itself downloads from the same
# dart-archive CDN `dart-lang/setup-dart` uses, so leg-local gate output
# matches CI gate output.
#
# Version-aware like setup/fa.sh: an installed-but-stale SDK is reinstalled on
# mismatch — pool VMs keep a PERSISTENT $HOME, so a presence-only check lets
# an ancient binary shadow the requested toolchain forever.
#
# Usage:
#   dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|<version>]  # default: .dart-version pin, else
#                                        # dart-lang/setup-dart detection, else stable
#   DART_VERSION=beta dart.sh
#   DART_INSTALL_DIR=... dart.sh         # default: ~/.dart-sdk (SDK lands at <dir>/dart-sdk)
#
# Network-free subcommands (unit-test surface — js/unit-tests/test_dartSetup.js):
#   dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|<version>]
#       print the resolved target/URL/layout as key=value — no download
#   dart.sh status
#       print installed=<version from the dart --version banner> ('' when absent)
#   dart.sh summary
#       print the leg-summary line (gh-1137): `toolchain: dart <version>
#       (CI: <pin>, match: yes/no)` — plus a loud warning line when the repo
#       has no pin at all, and a n/a skip line on non-Dart repos. No download.
set -eu

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/_common.sh"

DART_ARCHIVE="https://storage.googleapis.com/dart-archive"
DART_INSTALL_DIR="${DART_INSTALL_DIR:-${HOME}/.dart-sdk}"
SDK_HOME="${DART_INSTALL_DIR}/dart-sdk"
SDK_BIN="${SDK_HOME}/bin"

# ── Platform ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# dart-archive bundle naming: dartsdk-<os>-<arch>-release.zip (x64/arm64).
os_arch() {
  case "$(uname -s)" in
    Darwin) OS="macos" ;;
    Linux)  OS="linux" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported OS ($(uname -s)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
  case "$(uname -m)" in
    arm64|aarch64) ARCH="arm64" ;;
    x86_64)        ARCH="x64" ;;
    *) echo "❌ unsupported arch ($(uname -m)) for the dart-archive SDK bundle" >&2; exit 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ── Version probes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Installed version from the `dart --version` banner. Probes OUR managed
# install dir FIRST, then PATH — the cache-hit decision in do_install
# registers <SDK_BIN> on PATH and points DART_HOME at it, so it must describe
# the SDK this script owns, never a foreign dart (e.g. a Flutter-bundled one)
# that happens to sit on PATH. The banner capture takes the FULL version
# token — beta/dev banners are "3.14.0-315.1.beta (beta) …", and truncating at
# the first "-" would never equal the version channel_latest resolves, so the
# version-aware cache hit would never fire on non-stable channels.
installed_version() {
  local d=""
  if [ -x "${SDK_BIN}/dart" ]; then
    d="${SDK_BIN}/dart"
  elif command -v dart >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    d="$(command -v dart)"
  fi
  [ -n "${d}" ] || { echo ""; return 0; }
  "${d}" --version 2>&1 \
    | sed -n 's/^Dart SDK version: \([^ )]*\).*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# Latest concrete version of a channel (dart-lang/setup-dart resolves "latest"
# through the same VERSION file).
channel_latest() {
  curl -fsSL --max-time 30 "${DART_ARCHIVE}/channels/$1/release/latest/VERSION" \
    | sed -n 's/.*"version"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -1
}

# ── Version-file pin (gh-1137 step 1) ────────────────────────────────────────
# The repo's own pin convention beats the CI workflow line: a one-token
# .dart-version at the repo root (same muscle memory as .nvmrc/.java-version).
# The first live token wins — comment and blank lines are skipped, inline
# comments stripped, whitespace trimmed. Empty output = no pin.
repo_version_pin() {
  [ -f "${PWD}/.dart-version" ] || return 0
  awk '{ sub(/#.*/, ""); gsub(/^[[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+$/, ""); if (NF) { print; exit } }' \
    "${PWD}/.dart-version" 2>/dev/null
}

# ── Dart-repo gate (gh-1137) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The AUTO path (no explicit target anywhere) only makes sense on a repo that
# actually has Dart code — a pure JS/Kotlin repo leg must not pull a ~215 MB
# SDK it can never run. Echoes 1 (pubspec.yaml present) or 0.
is_dart_repo() {
  if [ -f "${PWD}/pubspec.yaml" ]; then
    echo "1"
  else
    echo "0"
  fi
}

# ── Loud stable-fallback warning (gh-1137 step 3) ────────────────────────────
# A Dart repo with NEITHER a version-file pin NOR a dart-lang/setup-dart line
# in CI resolves to stable — correct per contract, but local format/analyzer
# output is then NOT CI truth. Say so, loudly, before any download starts.
warn_unpinned_stable_fallback() {
  echo "⚠️⚠️  Dart SDK: no version pin found (no .dart-version, no dart-lang/setup-dart sdk:/channel: in .github/workflows) — falling back to stable" >&2
  echo "⚠️⚠️  LOCAL dart format/analyzer RESULTS MAY DIFFER FROM CI — pin the SDK (.dart-version or the CI workflow's setup-dart sdk: input) to make leg gates reproducible" >&2
}

# ── Quality-workflow detection ("same channel the repo's quality.yml uses") ──
# Scan the checked-out repo's workflows for the dart-lang/setup-dart step and
# read its with: inputs. Echoes "found|sdk|channel" (any field may be empty).
quality_detection() {
  local f kv found=0 sdk="" channel=""
  for f in "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yml "${PWD}"/.github/workflows/*.yaml; do
    [ -f "${f}" ] || continue
    while IFS= read -r kv; do
      case "${kv}" in
        step=*)    found=1 ;;
        sdk=*)     if [ -n "${kv#sdk=}" ] && [ -z "${sdk}" ]; then sdk="${kv#sdk=}"; found=1; fi ;;
        channel=*) if [ -n "${kv#channel=}" ] && [ -z "${channel}" ]; then channel="${kv#channel=}"; found=1; fi ;;
      esac
    done <<EOF
$(awk -v sq="'" '
  # Comment lines never contribute — neither a commented-out step
  # ("# - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@v1") nor a stale "# channel: beta" note.
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*#/ { next }
  # The step marker must be a live list item ("  - uses: …"), optionally with
  # a QUOTED action ref (uses: "dart-lang/setup-dart@v1" — legal YAML, common
  # in generated/templated workflows).
  /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*uses:[[:space:]]*"?(dart-lang\/setup-dart)/ { inb = 1; print "step=1"; next }
  inb && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*(name|uses|run):[[:space:]]/ { inb = 0 }
  inb && /sdk:/ {
    sub(/.*sdk:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "sdk=" $0
  }
  inb && /channel:/ {
    sub(/.*channel:[[:space:]]*/, ""); gsub(/["]/, ""); gsub(sq, "")
    sub(/[[:space:]]*#.*/, ""); gsub(/[[:space:]]/, ""); print "channel=" $0
  }
' "${f}" 2>/dev/null)
EOF
  done
  echo "${found}|${sdk}|${channel}"
}

# ── Usage ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
Usage: dart.sh [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]
            # default target: the repo's .dart-version pin, else the
            # quality.yml dart-lang/setup-dart channel/sdk detection, else
            # stable (+ loud warning) — skipped entirely on non-Dart repos
       DART_VERSION=<channel|version> dart.sh
       dart.sh plan [stable|beta|dev|latest|<version>]   # network-free preview
       dart.sh status                                    # installed version + dir
       dart.sh summary        # leg-summary line: toolchain: dart <v> (CI: <pin>, match: yes|no)
EOF
}
